bull_bear.body:
- The balance sheet is highly geared and has not deleveraged over five years: Net Debt of Rs 186 Cr (FY22), 346 (FY23), 437 (FY24), 421 (FY25), 439 (FY26).
- Net Debt to Equity (x) is disclosed as 2.1 (FY22), 3.3 (FY23), 3.9 (FY24), 3.5 (FY25), 3.7 (FY26).
- Returns have compressed steadily: ROCE 10.9% (FY22), 9.7% (FY23), 8.7% (FY24), 7.9% (FY25), 5.9% (FY26); RONW 12.9% (FY22), 16.3% (FY23), 10.0% (FY24), 6.8% (FY25), 2.0% (FY26).
- Working capital has been pulled down sharply: Net Working Capital of Rs 46 Cr (FY22), 38 (FY23), 39 (FY24), 36 (FY25), 22 (FY26); Fixed Asset Coverage Ratio 1.4x, 1.3x, 1.3x, 1.4x, 1.5x over FY22-FY26.
- Finance cost is a structural drag on the P&L, running at Rs 30.33 Cr for FY26 against FY26 EBITDA of Rs 49.83 Cr. The deck states no dividend policy, no repayment schedule and no deleveraging target.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Three-vertical presence is the stated basis of the franchise: "Our presence across suitings, furnishing fabrics and yarns provides a strong base to capture emerging opportunities" (Chairman's message).
- Export heritage is the core claim: "Among the first Indian companies to venture into suiting exports, BSL is today one of India's leading exporters of suiting fabrics."
- Furnishing is framed as the company's decade-plus growth engine: the deck describes "a decisive step to venture into furnishing fabrics, and over the last decade or more, this has been one of the key growth drivers for the company."
- The Chairman frames the industry backdrop as favourable - "India's textile industry is entering an encouraging phase, supported by the country's growing role in international sourcing, resilient exports and continued policy support" - while naming "cotton, raw-material and energy costs and changing trade policies" as the pressures requiring "continued agility".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Trade policy] Management ties the growth case to a widening FTA network: "The India-UK FTA provides a meaningful platform for new business, and we are confident of leveraging it through focused initiatives and suitable offerings" (Chairman), and "The India-New Zealand FTA, signed in April 2026, and the India-Oman CEPA further support this outlook, subject to their respective entry-into-force processes" (Managing Director).
- [Corporate history] Incorporated in 1970 under the name "Raj General Udyog Private Limited" and later "Converted into a Public Limited Company under the name of 'Bhilwara Synthetics Limited'"; the milestone slide's year markers (1970, 1976, 1971, Mid 80's, Mid 2000's, 2023) come through the extraction detached from their event text, so only the 1970 incorporation name is asserted here and the remaining year-to-event pairings are not.
- [Multi-year revenue trend] Revenue (Rs Cr) is charted as 436 (FY22), 472 (FY23), 666 (FY24), 667 (FY25), 657 (FY26) - i.e. flat-to-down for three years - with Gross Profit of 226, 251, 295, 298, 283 and Gross margin 51.6%, 53.0%, 44.2%, 44.6%, 43.0% over the same years, and EBITDA of 41, 52, 66, 60, 50 at margins of 9.5%, 11.1%, 9.9%, 9.0%, 7.6%.
- [Deck sections lost in extraction] Slides titled "About Us", "Strong Parentage", "Corporate Governance", "Growth Driving Factors", "Sustainability Initiatives", "Management Team", "Board Members" and "Our Achievements" appear as headings only, with no body text captured. Their absence here is an extraction gap, not a statement that BSL lacks such disclosure.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions BSL Limited as a long-established Bhilwara-lineage textile manufacturer spanning suitings, furnishing fabrics and yarns - "among the first Indian companies to venture into suiting exports" and "today one of India's leading exporters of suiting fabrics" - now pushing value addition, a widened product mix and overseas expansion off a heavily levered balance sheet.
